answer: Each identity keeps one ember lit by feeding it one fresh job receipt from the public record every epoch; an ember left cold restarts its standing from zero. Each epoch the beacon commits one seed, the prior epoch's public hash, published beforehand, so anyone can recompute which embers burn. Every claim bears its plume: a signature by the ember's own key over its latest feeding receipt and the current beacon seed, verifiable by any peer. A plume signed twice over one receipt is twin smoke, and both embers go out at once; keeping N heads lit takes N keys, N receipts, and N jobs every epoch.
